decisions.reason: Recasts the run-on into an em-dash aside and 'the real-world me,' which reads more naturally than BASE's separate clause while keeping the point.
'Huff, huff' is a cleaner, more natural rendering of the panting '헉, 허억' than BASE's mixed 'Gasp… Hah, hah.'
SOL's 'face and body were bruised and swollen' directly matches 멍들고 부어오른; BASE's abstract 'bruises and swelling covered' is stiffer.
BASE's 'enough breathing room' preserves 여유 (leisure/composure); SOL's 'enough energy' drops it and duplicates 'fresh as a daisy.'
'You can't fight that crudely' is punchier dialogue and closer to the dismissive 쓰나 than BASE's clunkier 'what good is fighting so crudely?'
SOL drops the translationese 'my body,' giving cleaner English with identical meaning to 몸을 움직일 수도.
'Watching it like this just pisses me off even more' reads more naturally and matches 보니까/더 better than BASE's 'Seeing it like this.'
'third-person perspective' is more idiomatic than 'third party's point of view,' and 'earlier fight' correctly includes 앞서.
Only the elongation placement differs; BASE's 'sooon' and SOL's 'biiitch' are equally faithful and equally natural.
'with a furious scream' captures the force of 악을 쓰며 more vividly than the bare 'screaming,' without adding meaning.
SOL drops the calqued 'With my movements growing wider, I was leaving' into direct past-tense prose matching 동작이 커지니 빈틈도 많다.
'flowing like water' is more natural than 'like water flowing,' and 'series of moments' renders 장면의 반복 cleanly.
'Bastard really can fight' is more natural thought-voice than BASE's comma-spliced 'Bastard, he can fight.'
'didn't recognize' is idiomatic for 알 수 없는, where BASE's 'couldn't understand' is a flatter gloss.
'a true martial artist of Murim' captures the emphasis of the quoted 무림인, which BASE renders flat.
'gotten cocky' and 'strong enough to hold my own' render 자만심 and 먹힐 more naturally than BASE's wordier 'too full of myself' and 'strength would get me somewhere.'
BASE's 'the kind of thought that gets you killed' is the standard set phrase and matches 죽기 딱 좋은 생각; SOL's 'thinking' is no better.
'celebrating' fits 희희낙락 (happy rejoicing) better than BASE's 'gloating,' and 'all that experience' reads more smoothly.
SOL's clause splits the two 각오 statements as the Korean does, avoiding BASE's awkward merge of both resolves into one sentence.
Restores the second Korean 각오 sentence ('F급 헌터가 아닌 무림인이 될 각오'), keeping the Murim/martial-artist/Hunter terminology BASE collapses into the prior line.
Both candidates drop the negation in 놔! 안 놔!, losing the demand-then-refusal beat; the repair preserves the source's two-part exchange.
decisions.replacement: Let go! I won't let go!

decisions.reason: 'only to rise again' is more elegant and natural than BASE's repetitive 'knocked down and getting back up.'
'I did land one good hit' preserves the affirming 지 tone of 결국 마지막에 한 방 먹였지 better than BASE's appended 'though.'
'The way I have for the past seven years' is smoother English for 지난 7년처럼 than BASE's 'Like I did.'
BASE's 'rose above' preserves the rising motion of 솟아올랐다; SOL's flat 'appeared' loses it.
SOL drops the source's leading dash on the System notice line; BASE preserves the source's formatting marker with no prose gain in SOL.
'to the System's voice' is more natural English than the redundant 'to the sound of the System's voice.'
'Are you awake' is the natural English equivalent of the formal 정신이 드십니까 in a waking/medical context.
'dressed in white' and 'A strange smell hung' render 흰옷을 걸친 and 감돌고 있었다 more idiomatically than BASE's 'man in white' and 'was filled.'
'read my mind' is a natural idiom for perceiving the unspoken 의문; BASE's 'noticed my question' is stiffer and no closer.
BASE keeps the archaic unit 'half a shichen,' preserving the beat where the narrator converts it to an hour in the next thought; SOL flattens that texture.
Joining the two clauses with a comma flows better than BASE's detached 'And this NPC was a physician.'
BASE keeps the shichen-to-hour conversion beat (반 시진 → 한 시간), which SOL's 'I was out for an hour?' erases.
'from the bruising' is a more idiomatic collocation than BASE's 'because of the bruises.'
'Once his footsteps had faded' is more concise natural prose than BASE's 'Once I heard his footsteps receding.'
Only difference is SOL stripping the source's leading dash on the instruction line; no prose improvement, so preserve BASE's source-faithful formatting.
SOL drops the added flourish 'sitting,' giving cleaner English closer to 그대로 남아 있다.
'After thinking for a moment' and SOL's 'After a moment's thought' are both faithful and equally natural for 잠시 고민하다가.
SOL restores the source image 모습 ('the sight of myself') and 떠올랐다 better than BASE's recast 'I'd remembered how.'
'soon' matches 이내 more precisely than SOL's 'quickly'; both read fine.
SOL's 'The gap … was that vast' is more direct and natural than BASE's convoluted 'That was how vast the gap … had been.'
BASE's 'as far as I was concerned' is closer to 내가 생각하기에 than SOL's perceptual 'as far as I could tell.'
'How could he react like that? Move like that?' is tighter and more natural than BASE's 'was he able to.'
BASE's emphatic 'did exist' preserves the concessive 긴 in 존재하긴 한다; SOL drops it.
BASE and SOL differ only by the article; 'martial arts here were' matches 이곳에서의 무공 and is no worse.
SOL's 'both practical and precise' improves BASE, but its singular 'It reminded me' clashes with plural 동작 하나하나; keep SOL's first sentence and BASE's plural subject.
decisions.replacement: Every movement was both practical and precise. They reminded me of interlocking gears driven by internal energy.

decisions.reason: The staccato 'Defeat. Death.' gives the punch of the Korean list and reads better than BASE's flat 'The words defeat and death.'
BASE preserves the '때였다' frame on the curse sentence and the intensity of 쌍욕; SOL drops both from this hunk.
Korean 문밖에서 인기척이 들려왔다 has no framing 'that was when'; BASE's plain 'I heard someone outside' is closer.
'before I could react' is more concise and natural than BASE's 'before I had a chance to react.'
BASE's progressive 'was glaring' matches the ongoing 눈빛을 쏟아내는 … 있었다 better than SOL's simple past.
'He has bruises' and SOL's 'some bruising' are equally faithful and natural for 타박상이 있지만.
'He should have broken a leg, at least' is more idiomatic active English than BASE's passive 'His leg should at least have been broken.'
BASE's 'threatening glare' matches 흉흉한; SOL's 'murderous' over-intensifies the look.
SOL's 'I had never seen this man … before' is a more direct construction than BASE's cleft 'He was a man … I had never seen before.'
'At least Level 30' avoids BASE's redundant, slightly contradictory 'Over Level 30, at minimum' for 최소 30레벨 이상.
SOL's relocated line adds the source's 무엇보다 ('More importantly'), which BASE omits.
'slap … across the mouth' is natural English for 아구창을 … 날려 버릴; 'smack' is no better and the restructure is faithful.
'If that hits me' is looser, more natural thought-English than BASE's 'If I took one hit from that.'
'at the sight of his palm, which was as large as a pot lid' reads more smoothly than BASE's comma-appended 'as large as a pot lid.'
BASE's 'the man looked dangerous in every way' and SOL's 'everything about him looked dangerous' are equally faithful for 전체적으로 그냥 위험하게 생겼다.
'stood nearly two meters tall' and 'sheathed in muscles' and 'cold gaze' are more vivid, idiomatic English than BASE's 'was nearly two meters tall / muscles wrapped around.'
SOL's 'murder was both his hobby and his specialty' cleans up BASE's awkward 'His hobby looked like murder, and his specialty probably was too.'
BASE's 'this man' / 'Where had I seen this man' and SOL's 'him' are both faithful for 이 아저씨를 어디서 봤더라.
'it would be more accurate to say' renders 진태경이 그를 닮았다고 해야 맞다 more precisely than BASE's 'the truth was that.'
BASE's 'trampling all over' preserves the crush metaphor of 깔아뭉개는 better than SOL's weaker 'walking all over.'
'eyes bulged' captures the angry wide-eyed force of 눈을 부릅떴다 better than BASE's neutral 'went wide.'
SOL's singular 'fist' matches 주먹 and 'Keeping a wary eye' more naturally renders 주의 깊게 바라보며 than BASE's plural 'fists' and 'watched carefully.'
SOL keeps the interrogative form of 그딴 소리가 나와? and reads spontaneously; BASE's 'How dare you say that to me!' flattens it.
'I'm very sorry if I got it wrong' captures the apologetic 정말 죄송합니다 more fully than BASE's 'I'm sorry if that wasn't it.'
BASE's 'chilly' matches 서늘한 and keeps it distinct from the earlier icy 싸늘한; SOL's 'icy' duplicates the stronger term.
'a desperate SOS' captures 간절한 … 구조 신호 crisply where BASE's 'urgent distress signal' is formal and flat.
Isolating 'Bang.' on its own line matches the standalone 쾅 and lands the beat before the hell-gate line.
'The door slamming shut' conveys the force implied by 쾅 better than BASE's neutral 'The door closing.'
SOL rightly keeps the man as subject but 'Alone with me in the room' is awkward; BASE adds an unsupported 'I watched as.' 'Alone together' fixes both.
decisions.replacement: Alone together in the room, the man raised his pot-lid-sized palm and began walking toward me.

decisions.reason: SOL's 'There's a limit to how much of a wastrel you can be!' matches the exclamatory force of the Korean better than BASE's flatter 'There's a limit to acting like a wastrel.'
'jumped to my feet' and SOL's 'leaped to my feet' are both faithful and natural for 벌떡 일어나.
BASE keeps 잘 ('explain everything properly'); SOL drops it and adds an unsupported 'so' to 'so angry.'
BASE's 'touch the wall' matches 등이 벽에 닿는; SOL's 'hit the wall' adds an impact not in the source.
SOL strips the source's leading dash on the Confusion notice; BASE preserves the source formatting marker.
'race to reach the egg' avoids BASE's fertilization/implantation mislabel (착상) and 'That had been rough' is more natural.
BASE keeps the '그 순간이었다' frame but drops 스르륵 and reverses the order; SOL keeps order and 'slowly' but loses the frame. Repair preserves both.
decisions.replacement: It was just as I thought of my family and slowly closed my eyes.

decisions.reason: BASE's 'whenever you get a chance' is the idiomatic rendering of 틈만 나면; SOL's 'the chance' implies a specific occasion.
SOL preserves the 입(mouth)-versus-손(hands) contrast in 분노…말들을 쏟아 내면서, 손은…, which BASE's 'He kept spewing' erases.
SOL removes the source's leading dash on the Fear notice; BASE keeps the source formatting marker.
BASE's 'family. A disgrace!' mirrors the Korean's comma-then-exclamation punctuation (수치다, 수치!) more closely than SOL's double exclamation.
SOL's 'certainly was feeling' captures the concessive 긴 하다 in 느끼고 있긴 하다 that BASE drops.
Optional complementizer 'that' does not affect meaning; BASE and SOL are equivalent.
'like those of a physician' matches 의사의 그것 (the doctor's hands) while BASE's 'moving like a physician' shifts the comparison.
BASE's 'the bruised areas' matches 타박상 부위 and 'Every time' matches 때마다 better than SOL's 'every bruise' and 'Whenever.'
SOL's dashes read better but 'you'll be in real trouble' weakens the threat 경을 칠 것이다; BASE's 'get what's coming to you' is right but choppier. Combine SOL's punctuation with BASE's phrase.
decisions.replacement: You little bastard! Keep acting like this and—huh? Huh!—you'll get what's coming to you. Do you understand?

decisions.reason: BASE's 'in a small voice' matches 작은 목소리 and its single-sentence structure matches the Korean; SOL's 'low voice' changes 작은 to 낮은.
Restores the whispered line (생각보다 경미해서 다행이다…) that BASE omits entirely.
SOL's 'One question, loaded with all kinds of meaning' renders 여러 가지가 함축된 한마디 more vividly than BASE's 'contained a great many things.'
'expression' and 'fawn' read more naturally than BASE's 'face' and 'baby deer' for 얼굴 … 아기 사슴.
BASE's 'Did it hurt your feelings?' and SOL's 'Did I hurt your feelings?' are equally faithful for 혹시 섭섭했던 거냐?
SOL's 'You know how dearly I raised you' matches the '알면서' (you-know) ending; BASE turns it into a question not in the source.
'must have hurt his head' matches 머리를 다쳤나 보네; BASE's 'hit his head' specifies an impact the Korean does not.
BASE adds 'missing' and SOL adds 'another,' both unsupported, and SOL drops 뒷모습; the repair keeps the retreating-figure image without adding a modifier.
decisions.replacement: As I watched his retreating figure, I suddenly felt that a piece of the puzzle had fallen into place.
